visual_review.identity: Deep warm brown ground with sparse muted olive-green and dry brown broadleaf groups, a few blunt twigs and gray-brown embedded stones. Broad open soil dominates; mixed green/brown identity survives.
visual_review.style_review: Much calmer and more broadly grouped than the original leaf carpet, with roughly ten to fourteen groups including edge-clipped groups. Leaf faces have two to four angular planes and some center-fold marks; soil retains faint low-contrast cloudy texture rather than absolutely flat graphic interiors. No neon, fine leaf carpet or added standing scenery.
visual_review.scale_caveat: A broad leaf group is around180-270 native pixels, about37-55 logical units at256 period; individual leaves often6-20 units. These are larger than scattered original fine litter. Compare actual forest-mask/scene scale before binding.
visual_review.native_acceptance: Opaque native candidate reviewed, no natural seamlessness or actual-scene acceptance claimed.

visual_review.identity: Subdued yellow-olive broadleaf litter on warm brown soil, sparse gray stones and longer angular branch/root segments. More yellow/ochre and visibly lighter than source1, preserving the source distinction.
visual_review.style_review: About twelve to sixteen leaf groups including clipped edge clusters, broad uncluttered ground and chunky faceted branches. Leaf center folds and some secondary faceting remain; soil retains faint cloudy texture. Branches are thicker and more object-like than original thin tracery but stay ground accents, without trees or standing props.
visual_review.scale_caveat: Most leaf groups are around180-260 native pixels, about37-53 units at256. Larger branched segments span roughly400-550 native pixels or82-112 world units, requiring actual masked scene review for scale.
visual_review.palette_caveat: Leaves are more golden ochre and slightly stronger in color than the original subdued yellow-olive litter. Exact color matching is not claimed.
visual_review.native_acceptance: Opaque native candidate only; no natural seamlessness or actual-scene acceptance claimed.
